page: Amazon Web Services g7.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, delivering 192 physical cores across 192 vCPUs with a single thread per core architecture. The host provides 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per physical core.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by eight NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 4500 GPUs, providing an aggregate of 256 GB of GPU VRAM. Storage architecture consists of 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and the instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 700 Gbps. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The dense co-location of 192 dedicated physical cores, eight Blackwell GPUs, 7,600 GB of local high-speed NVMe storage, and 700 Gbps network capacity provides high consolidated resource efficiency for large installations. It reduces multi-node overhead for workloads that fit within a single host boundary, balancing extreme compute and I/O density against substantial operational resource requirements.

This server type is engineered for heavy GPU-accelerated computing workloads, including large-scale graphics rendering, distributed machine learning inference, computer vision pipelines, and high-throughput data processing tasks that require extensive parallel compute, large fast local storage arrays, and high network throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services g7.48xlarge is a high-density accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 dedicated Intel x86_64 cores operating at 3.9 GHz without multi-threading, supported by 768.0 GB of system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 4500 GPUs yielding a cumulative 256 GB of VRAM. High-throughput data access and transit are facilitated by 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 700 Gbps. By combining 192 physical processing cores with eight enterprise GPUs and substantial local NVMe capacity, the g7.48xlarge offers significant qualitative compute density within a single node. This system profile fits distributed graphic pipelines, large-scale visual computing, batch rendering, parallel machine learning inference, and data-intensive workflows demanding high GPU parallelism and broad I/O bandwidth.
